events.summary: All three channels: 94.5% ± 5.0 vs 39.5% ± 15.1 for current practice (% of working parents who heard within 3 days). P4 has the highest reach: 94.5% ± 5.0 of working parents heard within 3 days versus 39.5% ± 15.1 under current practice, a gain of 55.0 percentage points. It also edges out the other tested options, beating P3 at 93.0% ± 6.8 and P2 at 91.0% ± 11.2 while keeping the best observed average and the tightest spread.
events.assumptions: The result depends on synthetic defaults for resident schedules, arrival patterns, and word-of-mouth rates, plus the model assumption that board and bulletin channels exist locally even though the provided sources only explicitly confirm the online channel. It also assumes the measured outcome in the completed runs generalizes to the held-out scenarios.
events.pilot: Run a 2-week live pilot using all three channels for one library notice cycle. Measure the share of working parents who report hearing the notice within 3 days, plus per-channel click/scan counts and any duplicate exposures, then compare against the prior online-only notices baseline.
